Subject: Light Up a Life 2026

Hilary asked on here last week whether we're doing the tree again this year. We are, Hilary, and I'm so glad you're bringing your sister.

Our Light Up a Life tree goes up in the shop window on Saturday 28 November, and we'll switch the lights on that afternoon at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are kindly coming back to sing three or four carols. Doreen is doing her mince pies again, so do come early if you want one.

Memory tags will be on the counter from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. You can write yours in the shop, or take an envelope home and bring it back when you're ready. Some people would rather do it quietly at the kitchen table, and that's perfectly all right.

Every name on the tree will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You're very welcome to come, but you don't have to be there for your name to be read. We read all of them either way.

The tree isn't only for hospice families. It's for anyone who is missing someone, whether they died last month or forty years ago, at the hospice or anywhere else. Husbands, wives, mums, dads, children, friends, the next-door neighbour who always took your parcels in. If they mattered to you, they belong on the tree.

You don't need to buy a tag, either. If you'd simply like to come in and stand by the tree for a few minutes, please do. Nobody will ask you for anything, and nobody will hurry you. That's what it's there for.

I'll say a little about my own tag, because it's been on my mind. My husband Ray died at the hospice seven years ago this month. The first year I put his name on the tree, I could hardly hold the pen. It took me most of an afternoon to write three letters. These days I write it at the counter in between customers, with the same pen, and then I hang it up and go back to pricing paperbacks. I don't miss him any less. It has just become part of the year, and of the shop, and of all the other names hanging alongside his. I mention it only in case this is your first year and it feels like too much. It does get a little easier to write. Not easier to miss them, but easier to write.

Last year there were 412 names on our tree, and Sandra at the hospice tells me your tags helped keep the night sitters going for most of a month. That means families getting some sleep while someone sat up with the person they love. Thank you to everyone who wrote a tag, came to the switch-on, sang, baked, stood in the cold on Magdalen Street, or just stopped by the window on their way past.

We'll keep the tree lit until Twelfth Night. Do come and see it.

Jean
